Cross-Validated Class Enumeration

cv_enumeration.Rd

Selects the number of latent classes in random-effects mixture meta-analysis using K-fold cross-validation. Candidate models are compared based on their out-of-sample negative log predictive density (NLPD).

Usage

cv_enumeration(x, folds = 5L)

Arguments

x

An object for which a method exists, typically a mixture_list of at least two fitted remix models with different numbers of latent classes. The models must be based on the same observations and use the same constraints on class-specific means and heterogeneity variances. Models should be ordered by increasing number of classes, starting with a one-class model.

folds

Integer. Number of cross-validation folds. Defaults to 5. Must be between 2 and the number of observations.

Value

A list containing:

best_class

Integer index of the candidate model with the lowest total cross-validated negative log predictive density. If models are ordered from one to the maximum number of classes, this index corresponds to the selected number of classes.

scores

Named numeric vector containing the total negative log predictive density across folds for each candidate model.

fold_scores

Numeric matrix containing the negative log predictive density for each fold (rows) and candidate model (columns).

fold_id

Integer vector indicating the fold assigned to each observation.

Details

The function randomly partitions the observations into folds approximately equal-sized subsets. For each candidate number of classes, the model is re-estimated on the training observations and evaluated on the held-out observations using the negative log predictive density. Smaller values indicate better out-of-sample predictive performance.

The negative log predictive densities are summed across folds for each candidate model. The model with the smallest total score is selected.

The mean and heterogeneity variance constraints are inferred from the second model in x and applied consistently to all models fitted during cross-validation.

Because fold assignments are random, results may differ between calls. Use set.seed() before calling the function to obtain reproducible fold assignments and random starting values.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(metamixture)

set.seed(123)

# Simulate meta-analytic data
dat <- sim_remix_fixed_tau(n = 100, es = 2)

# Estimate candidate models
models <- lapply(1:3, function(k) {
remix(
  yi = dat$yi,
  vi = dat$vi,
  classes = k,
  tau2 = "equal"
)
})

# Five-fold cross-validation
cv <- cv_enumeration(models, folds = 5)

# Selected number of classes
cv$best_class

# Total predictive scores
cv$scores

# Scores by fold and candidate model
cv$fold_scores
} # }
